Lactulose mechanism

A patient with overt hepatic encephalopathy is treated with lactulose. Colonic bacteria metabolize this poorly absorbed disaccharide and lower luminal pH. Which effect contributes to reduced absorption of intestinal ammonia during treatment?

  1. Conversion of all ammonia into oxygen
  2. Direct inhibition of brain dopamine receptors
  3. Complete sterilization of the bloodstream
  4. Stimulation of renal ammonium absorption as its principal action
  5. Conversion of NH3 to less absorbable NH4+
Answer and explanation

Conversion of NH3 to less absorbable NH4+

Luminal acidification favors ammonium formation; catharsis also promotes nitrogen elimination.

Option explanations

Conversion of NH3 to less absorbable NH4+: Luminal acidification favors ammonium formation; catharsis also promotes nitrogen elimination.

Conversion of all ammonia into oxygen: This is not a biochemical effect of lactulose.

Direct inhibition of brain dopamine receptors: Lactulose acts mainly within the bowel.

Complete sterilization of the bloodstream: Lactulose is not a systemic antibiotic.

Stimulation of renal ammonium absorption as its principal action: The described mechanism is intestinal acidification.
